verdict.difficultyReason: Required review takes weeks. This holds whatever the unknown details turn out to be.
verdict.useCase: A multi-tenant AI agent that reads and posts messages in its customers' Slack workspaces (a distributed app using bot and user scopes such as channels:history).

timeToCredentials.basis: Our estimate: creating an app needs a Slack account and a workspace (the walkthrough had to create a new free workspace), after which the Client ID is visible at once; no source gives a time.

timeToProduction.basis: About 12 weeks at most: Slack's review guide says preliminary feedback takes up to 10 business days and functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps); turnaround varies with volume, and the estimate is shown on the submission page. An app must also first be installed on 10 or more active workspaces.

humanEffortHours.basis: Our estimate: configuring the app and OAuth flow, preparing Marketplace submission materials, and handling reviewer feedback; no source gives effort figures.

verdict.summary: Slack lets you create an app with an account and a workspace. Slack's distribution docs describe a checklist and an Activate Public Distribution button with no review step (not attempted in our walkthrough), but Slack says commercial distribution should go through the Marketplace, which has a manual review of up to roughly 12 weeks.
verdict.biggestLaunchRisk: Slack Marketplace review is manual, cannot be sped up, requires all feedback to be addressed, and needs the app to have 10 or more active workspaces before submission. Without approval, new unlisted commercial apps face a much lower conversations.history rate limit (1 request/min, 15 objects), which would cripple an agent that reads messages.

specialRequirements: Compliance with Slack Marketplace app guidelines and policies (for Marketplace listing)

managedCovers.text: Composio lists Slack under Composio-managed OAuth, so a shared Composio OAuth app may be usable for prototyping without registering your own Slack app.

youNeedOwnWhen.text: You want your own branding, client ID and secret for a distributed multi-tenant product. Sources do not detail what Composio's managed app covers, so this is inferred.
You want to commercially distribute the app: Slack says the Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercial distribution, which requires your own app.
You need Marketplace-level rate limits for conversations.history and conversations.replies; non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps get 1 request/min and 15 objects per request.
You need a Marketplace listing with your own developer, terms of service and privacy details shown to customers' admins.

requirements.text: A Slack account is not enough: creating an app also needs a workspace, and the apps page asks for its own sign-in. A new free workspace worked. The Client ID is visible at once; the secrets stay masked behind Show. (Docs said: A Slack account to create the app and reach the App Management page, where the client ID is found.)

requirements.text: HTTPS OAuth redirect URLs, required scopes configured, and no hard-coded tokens before activating public distribution.
For a Marketplace listing: follow Slack's Marketplace app guidelines and policies; Slack won't list apps that don't.
For Marketplace listing: developer details, terms of service and privacy and data governance information (e.g. data retention and deletion policies) appear on listings.
Whether a registered legal entity or verified business is required is not stated in the sources.

To submit to the Marketplace the app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces (active means used in the past 28 days); apps with fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users are below the minimum.

steps.detail: Sign in with a Slack account and open the App Management page, where you create the app and find its client ID.

steps.title: Create the app and configure bot and user scopes
steps.detail: Create the app and choose the minimum scopes it needs, for example channels:history. Bot scopes go in `scope=` and user scopes in `user_scope=`. Repeat installs add scopes to the token and scopes cannot be removed from an existing token.
steps.agentPrep: List the minimum bot and user scopes and a justification for each.

steps.title: Add HTTPS redirect URLs and implement the v2 OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id and scopes, receive the temporary code, then exchange it with your client secret for an access token. Store tokens per workspace.
steps.agentPrep: Draft the authorize URL builder and the code-exchange handler with per-workspace token storage.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.estimate: minutes to 1 hour (our estimate, not documented)
steps.detail: Until distribution is enabled, installing in another workspace returns invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app. Slack's distribution docs describe completing the checklist and clicking Activate Public Distribution, and mention no review step; a third party says it takes effect immediately. Activation was not attempted in our walkthrough.

steps.title: Test installation from a different workspace
steps.detail: Install from a workspace other than the one used for development. Optionally use a Slack Developer Program sandbox for building and testing at no extra cost.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace submission materials
steps.detail: Read the Marketplace guidelines and policies, and prepare listing details, terms of service, privacy and data governance information (retention and deletion policies).
steps.agentPrep: Draft the listing description, privacy and data retention text, and a scope justification checklist.

steps.title: Submit the app to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Submit from the submission page in your app settings, which also shows the estimated review turnaround.

steps.title: Wait for review and address feedback
steps.estimate: Up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback, then up to 10 weeks for functional review (new submissions)
steps.detail: Slack gives feedback in the submission flow and all feedback must be addressed before listing. It says it cannot skip or accelerate review to match your launch, and advises submitting as early as you can.

steps.title: Plan for customer workspace app approval
steps.detail: Workspace Owners can turn on app approval, so customers' admins may need to approve your app before members can install it.
steps.agentPrep: Write a short admin-facing note explaining the app, its scopes and data handling.

scopesAndNuances.text: Bot scopes use `scope=` and user scopes use `user_scope=` on the authorize URL; an app may request either or both.
Scopes are additive across installs for the same token, and you cannot remove scopes from an existing token without further steps (the source text is cut off).
Sign in with Slack user scopes cannot be combined with non-SIWS scopes in one OAuth flow; each set needs its own flow.

For commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace, created on or after May 29, 2025 (earlier apps from June 30, 2025 for net new installations; existing installations unaffected), conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request/min and a maximum and default `limit` of 15 objects. Marketplace apps are not affected.
Internal customer-built (custom) apps keep 50+ requests/min and up to 1,000 objects for these methods, but that is for a customer's own internal app, not a multi-tenant product.

Slack's changelog says the Slack Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing apps built with Slack APIs, and the distribution docs say apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing. Check the full API Terms of Service against your business model.
By default, members can install apps without Owner approval, but Workspace Owners can require pre-approval.
